title: Execution binding
description: What each task in a backlog binds its executor to read: the references with their versions, the facts already established, the inferences permitted without record, and what the task must preserve. It exists so context is a recorded input rather than a search result — two runs of one task otherwise read different documents. Every reference carries a version, which is what lets a delivery be traced to the text it was built from. `unresolved` is where a fact the specification does not settle goes; writing it into known_context instead would deliver an invention to the executor with the authority of a stated fact, and that is the failure the field exists to prevent.

binding_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

backlog_id.description: The backlog whose tasks these bind. A binding that cannot name its backlog binds tasks nobody can resolve.

bindings.description: One entry per task in the backlog, including a task that needs nothing. An empty binding states the task was considered; an absent one is indistinguishable from a task nobody bound.

section.description: The part of the document, not the whole of it. A reference to a file is a reference to whatever it says next week.

version.description: The document's version at binding time, its revision identifier where it has no version, or the literal 'unversioned'. Never omitted: without it a delivery cannot be traced to the text it was built from.

source.description: Where the fact came from. Required: an unsourced fact here is a rumour carrying the authority of the binding.

assumptions_allowed.description: Inference the executor may make without recording it. Short and specific: a broad permission here is how an executor's invention becomes invisible. Empty means every inference is recorded.

constraints.description: What this task must preserve because something outside it depends on it. Recorded on both sides where two tasks touch one component.

unresolved.description: What the task needs and the specification does not settle. Naming it is not solving it.
